newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU/Boeing make progress on one issue - EU source.
newsitem.headline: EU/Boeing make progress on one issue - EU source.

text.p: The European Commission and Boeing have made progress on one issue in their discussions on the aircraft manufacturer's planned merger with McDonnell-Douglas, an EU source said on Monday.
"Some progress has been made on one of the issues," the source said, but more progress needed to be made before the EU could clear the deal.
The source said he was not allowed to say which issue he was referring to. "Altogether more progress needs to be made, to put if mildly...", he added.
Earlier, the U.S. aerospace giant also said progress had been made, but no deal reached, in weekend talks with the Commission on the planned merger.
"We made progress," James Frank, Boeing's European executive vice president for government and public affairs said. "We still are optimistic that we will find a mutually acceptable solution,"

The Commission argues that the merger would add to Boeing's already dominant position in the aircraft industry. Among its other concerns, it opposes Boeing's exclusive contracts to supply aircraft to airlines such as Delta, American and Continental.
It also worries about the possibility of spillovers of public money, earmarked for research and development in defence, into Boeing's civil aviation business.
